title: ME07a: The Leadership Liminality Trap
author: Richard Claydon
summary: Told through the fictional leader Maya, this installment argues that modern flat organisations make people do two jobs at once, a vertical delivery role and a horizontal alignment role. Claydon names the resulting strain the Leadership Liminality Trap: people lead beyond their level without the title, support or legitimacy of that level. Without a developmental map, stretch feels like incompetence and organisations misread threshold states as performance problems. Maya's third rule is to calibrate for your level and anticipate the next, treating friction as a developmental signal. Reflection prompts for self, role and system close the piece.
points: Flat organisations structurally give people both a vertical team role and a horizontal cross-system role, doubling the strain.
The old linear ladder of promotion no longer fits, because people absorb complexity from the next level while being judged on the current one.
Without a map, stretch, drift, break and leap are misread as incompetence, disengagement, failure and arrogance.
Organisations pay for invisible thresholds by rewarding smoothness over substance and losing capable people.
The rule to calibrate for your level and anticipate the next reframes friction as a developmental signal.
quotes: Today, people are constantly leading beyond their level without the title, support, or legitimacy of that level. They’re already accountable for complexity they haven’t been prepared to hold.
What looks like inconsistency or contradiction in performance isn’t personal. It’s positional. It’s the strain of being asked to live in between levels, without scaffolding.

When threshold states are invisible, companies misread them as performance problems. They reward smoothness over substance, compliance over coherence. They lose good people who assume they don’t belong.
In Maya’s words: “People aren’t failing. They’re being failed—by systems that expect leadership without preparing for it.
The point isn’t to master the next level overnight. It’s to see it coming. To feel its pull. To develop just enough awareness to grow into it, even while delivering at your current one.
